root_cause.text: In dm-verity-fec, fec_decode_bufs() incorrectly assumed the first Reed-Solomon codeword’s parity bytes would always be fully contained within a single parity block, so its parity-buffer offset/block-transition logic could read past the end of the dm_bufio parity block buffer when roots and block alignment caused a codeword to span blocks.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “fec_decode_bufs() assumes that the parity bytes of the first RS codeword it decodes are never split across parity blocks” and gives the 4096-byte block, roots=17, nbufs=1 example where only 16 bytes remain but 17 are needed, causing “out-of-bounds from the parity block buffer”; the patch removes fec_read_parity()/par_buf_offset handling and replaces it with explicit parity_pos/to_copy logic that copies across block boundaries safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the local fec_read_parity() helper to consolidate or relocate parity-read logic without introducing new behavior in this hunk.
intent_record.what: The change deletes the entire static inline helper function fec_read_parity(), including its comment block, local variable declarations, parity-position calculation, conditional index increment when par_buf_offset is set, offset assignment, dm_bufio_read_with_ioprio() call, error logging, and buffer nulling on read failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime this file no longer provides the fec_read_parity() helper, so parity-block reading logic must now be handled elsewhere or no longer be used from this location; this removes the local wrapper around parity read calculation and error handling rather than adding new behavior in the shown hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix FEC parity block lookup so decoding reads the correct starting parity location across block boundaries and logs detailed read failures.
intent_record.what: The code removes the call to fec_read_parity() that returned a parity pointer and block offset, deletes the unused par_buf_offset initialization, replaces the old offset variable with parity_pos and adds to_copy and parity_block variables, computes parity_block and parity_pos directly from rsb, block_offset, v->fec->roots, v->fec->io_size, and v->data_dev_block_bits, reads parity data with dm_bufio_read_with_ioprio(), and adds an explicit DMERR log message before returning on read failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, parity block selection is now calculated explicitly so decoding starts from the correct parity block and byte position even when the number of FEC roots does not align to the I/O block size, including cases where parity bytes cross block boundaries. It also reports parity read failures with more specific diagnostic information instead of just propagating the error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix FEC parity buffering to correctly read Reed-Solomon parity bytes across parity block boundaries and handle follow-on parity read failures.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a single loop that copied parity bytes from `par[offset + j]` into `par_buf[par_buf_offset + j]` with logic that computes `to_copy = min(v->fec->io_size - parity_pos, v->fec->roots)`, copies available parity bytes from the current parity block into `par_buf`, and, if fewer than `roots` bytes remain, advances `parity_block`, resets `parity_pos`, releases the current buffer, reads the next parity block with `dm_bufio_read_with_ioprio`, checks for read errors, and copies the remaining parity bytes from the new block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this allows parity data needed for Reed-Solomon decoding to span across parity block boundaries instead of assuming all required `roots` bytes are contiguous in the current block. It prevents incorrect parity-buffer filling near the end of a parity block and adds error handling for the extra parity-block read, improving correctness of FEC decoding.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove in-loop parity offset advancement and next-block parity reads from fec_decode_bufs() to change parity-buffer traversal during FEC decoding.
intent_record.what: A block of code inside fec_decode_bufs() was removed from the loop after incrementing block_offset. The deleted code advanced the parity-data offset, handled the case where parity bytes span two blocks by copying a partial block into par_buf, released the current buffer when the offset reached the end of the current I/O block, and read the next parity block with fec_read_parity().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the loop no longer updates parity-buffer state or switches to the next parity block at that point in execution. This prevents the function from consuming additional parity bytes or fetching another parity buffer within this removed path, changing how parity data is traversed during FEC decoding.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix FEC parity reading during Reed-Solomon decoding so parity bytes are fetched from the correct locations across parity block boundaries and read failures are handled/logged properly.

relevance_review.reason: This change only removes/refactors the local fec_read_parity() helper and does not address the parity-buffer offset/block-boundary logic in fec_decode_bufs() that caused out-of-bounds reads.

The changes directly address the root cause in fec_decode_bufs(): they fix parity block/offset calculation and boundary-crossing logic so Reed-Solomon parity bytes are read correctly across parity block boundaries, preventing out-of-bounds reads from the parity block buffer.

The change directly modifies fec_decode_bufs() parity-buffer traversal by removing the in-loop offset advancement and next-block parity reads that were part of the incorrect block-transition logic causing out-of-bounds reads when a codeword’s parity spanned blocks.

candidates.rationale: This initial parity read uses par_buf_offset fixed at 0, embodying the incorrect assumption that the first codeword's parity starts in a way that does not require cross-block adjustment. That wrong starting location setup is central to the out-of-bounds parity access later.

This loop copies parity bytes under the assumption that roots - par_buf_offset bytes are available contiguously from the current parity block buffer. When the codeword parity spans a block boundary unexpectedly, this iteration range drives reads past the end of the buffer.

This is the direct out-of-bounds read site: it indexes par[offset + j] without ensuring the requested parity bytes remain within the current dm_bufio parity block buffer when a codeword spans parity blocks.

This boundary check only handled later in-loop split cases and reflects the faulty logic that split parity handling was needed only after advancing offset, not for the initial codeword parity location. That incomplete condition is part of the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct out-of-bounds access. It reads parity bytes from the current dm_bufio parity block buffer using par[offset + j] without ensuring those bytes are still within that block when the Reed-Solomon codeword's parity spans a block boundary.

This loop bound assumes that v->fec->roots - par_buf_offset parity bytes are contiguously available from the current parity block. When the initial parity location is near the end of a block, this iteration count drives the subsequent buffer access past the end of the dm_bufio buffer.

This initial parity read setup is part of the flawed starting-location logic. It embodies the incorrect assumption that the first codeword's parity can be read starting from the selected block/offset state without needing initial cross-block adjustment.

This condition reflects the incomplete split-handling logic: it only considered parity crossing a block boundary in a later case, not for the initial codeword parity placement. That incomplete assumption contributed to the incorrect traversal that enabled the out-of-bounds read.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it contains the parity-buffer offset and block-transition logic identified in the root cause. In `fec_decode_bufs()`, the code copies parity bytes for decode with `for (j = 0; j < v->fec->roots - par_buf_offset; j++) par_buf[par_buf_offset + j] = par[offset + j];` and later handles split parity only with `if (offset < v->fec->io_size && (offset + v->fec->roots) > v->fec->io_size) { par_buf_offset = v->fec->io_size - offset; ... } else par_buf_offset = 0;`. This logic still assumes the remaining parity bytes can be read contiguously from `par[offset + j]` up to `v->fec->roots - par_buf_offset`, based on a split calculation tied to `v->fec->roots` rather than correctly tracking when a codeword spans parity blocks. That is exactly the vulnerable construct described: parity-buffer offset/block-transition handling that can read past the end of the current dm_bufio parity block buffer when roots and block alignment make the codeword span blocks. The commit message is only about avoiding a double copy (`Avoid copying RS parity bytes twice`), and the diff merely changes from `u8` temp storage plus `fec_decode_rs8()` to direct `uint16_t` filling and direct `decode_rs8()` call. It does not introduce any new bounds-safe block transition handling. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present and the fix is not present.

The root cause was that parity bytes for a Reed-Solomon codeword could span two parity blocks, but the old logic assumed they were fully available in one dm-bufio block and could therefore access `&par[offset]` past the end of the current block buffer. In this commit, `fec_decode_bufs()` introduces explicit split handling: it adds `par_buf_offset = 0` and a local `par_buf[...]`, copies available bytes with `memcpy(&par_buf[par_buf_offset], &par[offset], v->fec->roots - par_buf_offset);`, and passes `par_buf` to `fec_decode_rs8()` instead of directly passing `&par[offset]`.
